channel.title: sgit.ai — updates
channel.description: What changed on sgit and on this site, as it happens.

item.title: The shorts page rewritten for someone who arrives with no context
item.description: A page of videos is a landing page whether or not it was designed as one. Traffic reaches the seven shorts from a feed, lands on it directly, and has never seen the vault, this site, or the argument. What sat above the seven players yesterday was an apology ab…

item.title: The build brief for putting a vault's decks on a website
item.description: Two releases documented this from the inside: reading one file out of a vault explains the mechanism, and the deck pages demonstrate it. Neither told another agent how to do it to their vault. That brief now exists. It follows the shape of the telemetry brief…

item.title: Seven shorts on the Licence to Operate vault — indexed, and put in the right order
item.description: The author recorded seven vertical videos walking through the Licence to Operate vault. None of them was on the site. They now have a page, collected in the order they are meant to be watched rather than the order a feed shows them: The mechanism (1–3) — grant…

item.title: The second build brief, and it mostly says don't build it
item.description: Two of the most common things an agent is asked to add to a vault are a markdown viewer and a file/folder browser with raw views . Both already exist in the vault platform, and most requests for them are answered by publishing files in the right shape and writ…

item.title: Decks and PDFs read straight out of a vault — with the viewer owned by the site
item.description: The vaults publish presentations. Four of them sit in the AIUC 1 conformance vault and five in Licence to Operate, and until this release the only way to see one was to open the vault's own app and drive it. They now play on the vault pages themselves, fetched…

item.title: A page per deck, a focus mode, and a vault catalogue an agent can read
item.description: Yesterday's release put the decks on the vault pages. Three things were missing, and this release adds them. A page per deck. Each of the nine published decks now has one — four under the AIUC 1 conformance vault, five under Licence to Operate. A deck page ope…

item.title: Two new sections — the team, written for the agents; and investors, in the open
item.description: The team is the agentic section: how this site is run by one person and a team of AI agents, written for the agents. A new agent should be able to read that page and one role page and begin. Nine roles, each a file. Sherpa, Publisher, Auditor, Journalist, Cart…

item.title: The proof moved up — the homepage, rebuilt to show vaults before it explains them
item.description: The homepage is rebuilt, following the diagnosis published this morning rather than a fresh opinion — and the "after" article puts each new band beside a screenshot of what it replaced, so the comparison is honest rather than flattering. The first screen now s…

item.title: The diagnosis before the rebuild — and a card for pointing at the sibling sites
item.description: Asked to step back and say how this site should present its twenty five published vaults, the answer was a diagnosis rather than a redesign — and it is published first, as an article with screenshots of the current site, so the rebuild that follows can be comp…

item.title: The board moves into a vault of its own — and its read key is published
item.description: Two releases after the board appeared as files in the site repository, the shape was right and the home was wrong: moving a card from review to done cost a full site release — build, validate, two pushes, and a wait for the deploy to verify. A board should be…

item.title: Our build brief was wrong, and the team that owns the code said so precisely
item.description: Two days ago v0.2.55 published a build brief on getting telemetry out of a vault whose read key is public. An agent built a vault from it and could not get events out. The SG/API team read the append lane code against our page and returned a line referenced re…

item.title: Ask this site — a pane on every page whose model calls tools over the site's own content
item.description: Every page now carries a pane, bottom right: Ask this site . It follows the three tiers the network chooser set out, with one difference that matters — the model does not read a catalogue pasted into its prompt. It is given seven tools and calls them. | Tool |…

item.title: The brief came back as a vault — and it is the first one here that phones home
item.description: v0.2.55 published a build brief on getting telemetry out of a vault whose read key is public. Another agent read it and shipped the thing, so two games about agent permissions now joins the published vaults — two deterministic games about grants, permissions a…

item.title: Briefs gets a second kind — references written to be executed, not asks waiting on a reply
item.description: Briefs has been a single scroll of cross team asks since v0.1.13 — each addressed to another team, each carrying a status, each closing when it is answered. A brief arrived this week that is a different species, so the page now says so and separates them. Buil…

item.title: Provenance is not conformance — the AIUC-1 vault, forked and layered
item.description: Provenance is not conformance joins the published vaults. It is a fork of the AIUC 1 catalogue vault that keeps every byte of it and adds one directory above it — 649 files against the catalogue's 135. Both vaults stay published, and the catalogue page now say…

item.title: The directory answers questions now — and the default tier needs no key
item.description: Two things: the network directory grew a chat box, and a second conference vault went up. Ask it which of the nineteen sites is yours. Type "I have to sign off a risk" and it points at risks.sgit.ai — and shows you the words it matched on. It runs in your brow…

item.title: An insurance policy for an agent — and the delta is the risk
item.description: Licence to Operate joins the published vaults — one agent, its policy, and a simulated conversation where every reply carries its price. The idea worth stealing is the delta. Three sets: CAN DO — the grant. 12 capabilities. MAY DO — the mandate. 4, and the onl…

item.title: A standard as a graph, and the one line that makes it trustworthy
item.description: AIUC 1, as a graph you can cite joins the published vaults — an unofficial, derivative machine readable catalog of the public AIUC 1 agent standard. It is not approved, certified or endorsed by AIUC, and the page carries that in a box above everything else rat…

item.description: The VoiceDebrief pitch to Founder Institute joins the published vaults — the 23rd, and not a deck about a vault but a deck presented from one. A presenter, not a PDF. Twelve slides with per slide target timings, a live 3:00 countdown, speaker notes, Focus and…
